note: Blocking ISA gate baseline for build-dos.ps1. Every i486 release, benchmark and instrumentation variant is recorded at zero above-i486 instructions. The i386 variant records the remaining i486 instructions. Any new or increased above-target encoding, any unclassified instruction, or any non-exempt P6 instruction fails the build.
variantKey: <cpuTarget>/<executableName>, where executableName is quake.exe (release), qbench.exe (-Benchmark), or qprof.exe (-Instrumentation). One figure per target is not enough: -Benchmark compiles the test-owned BENCH486 harness and -Instrumentation compiles the PROFILE486 counters, so those builds have their own instruction mix.

hardRules.exemptionReason: The CRC constant table lives in .text and disassembles as if it were instructions; its single decoded byte pattern is a p6 MMX opcode. It is data, not code, and is the only exemption in the tree.

buildDeterminism: The i486 release build audit on 2026-10-06 counted 168459 object instructions; total instruction counts are informational and can vary with compiler output. The gate compares per-encoding above-target counts after excluding 62/63 string-data decodes and the named CRC constant-table exemption. Builds audit only the explicit active object list because directories can retain stale objects from other selector sets. The i486 release, benchmark and instrumentation variants each have zero above-target instructions; the i386 variant has 141 i486 instructions.
scopeNote: tools/isa-audit.ps1 disassembles active build objects and counts inlined copies; tools/isa-audit-source.py independently classifies compiler-generated and preprocessed source instructions. The source and object totals differ because the object audit counts inlined copies and both audits handle data embedded in .text differently. Both now confirm zero above-i486 instructions for the i486 builds. IMUL 0F AF is an i386 instruction per the Intel 80386 manual.

noiseEncodings.note: 62 (bound) and 63 (arpl) are string literals, not instructions. DJGPP emits string data into .text, so objdump decodes it as code: 62 61 64 is 'ad', 63 6b 20 is 'ck ', 65 63 74 00 is 'ect' plus a NUL. They appear across ~50 objects and cannot be exempted by symbol the way crc.obj:_crctable is. The gate excludes them from enforcement and prints them instead, because they are the only two buckets whose count tracks message text rather than instructions. This is the same defect tools\isa-audit-source.py was written to avoid, at source level. It does not affect the i486 variants at all, because arpl and bound are i486 instructions: only the i386 gate sees them.

encodingMeanings.0f af: imul r32, r/m32 -- documented by the Intel 80386 manual; this was previously misclassified as Pentium.
encodingMeanings.0f 0b: ud2 -- unsupported on the 486; GCC emitted this in cold error paths until the per-source null-pointer behavior flags were added.
encodingMeanings.0f 30: wrmsr -- removed with the unreferenced StartMSRInterval/EndMSRInterval routines from dosasm.s.
encodingMeanings.0f 32: rdmsr -- removed with the unreferenced StartMSRInterval/EndMSRInterval routines from dosasm.s.
